title: UI Screenshot System
description: High-fidelity app, web, dashboard, and social interface prompts.
useWhen: Use for app screens, dashboards, social screenshots, and live interface mockups.
guidance: Lock platform, aspect ratio, layout hierarchy, and exact visible text.
Specify UI chrome such as status bars, tabs, action rows, or comment layers.
pitfalls: Avoid vague platform names and generic app mockups.
Constrain text readability and platform-specific details.

title: Infographic Engine
description: Structured diagrams, timelines, knowledge maps, and explainers.
useWhen: Use for explainer graphics, technical diagrams, timelines, and knowledge cards.
guidance: Define 3-5 modules, information flow, visual hierarchy, and short labels.
Use color groups, arrows, icons, and clean spacing to reduce clutter.
pitfalls: Avoid long paragraphs inside the image.
Limit module count before adding visual detail.

title: Scientific Scale Diagram
description: Multi-scale science visuals with readable labels and hierarchy.
useWhen: Use when the topic needs micro-to-macro scale comparison and labeled detail windows.
guidance: Use 6-8 scale frames and keep each label short.
Show units, magnification, and distinct scale detail.
pitfalls: Avoid making every scale frame visually identical.
Avoid generic magnifying glass icon layouts.

title: Poster Layout System
description: Event, product, movie, and social poster compositions.
useWhen: Use for event posters, movie posters, covers, and social campaign visuals.
guidance: Lock subject, headline, layout, palette, and aspect ratio.
Make the title hierarchy and primary visual clear.
pitfalls: Avoid mixed moodboards or process sheets when asking for one finished poster.
Constrain extra text and decorative symbols.

title: Sports Campaign Poster
description: Commercial sports visuals with athletes, props, and brand color.
useWhen: Use for sports brand campaigns, athlete posters, and product-led sport visuals.
guidance: Define sport, athlete pose, hero prop, title, and brand palette.
Use dramatic light, clean composition, and readable data overlays.
pitfalls: Avoid wrong equipment and noisy collage.
Keep the athlete and hero prop visually dominant.

title: Conceptual Typography Poster
description: Premium title-led posters with strong typographic systems.
useWhen: Use when the exact title must become the main visual structure.
guidance: Make typography the hero and spell the title exactly.
Tie human figures, objects, or landscapes to the title meaning.
pitfalls: Avoid default word art, unrelated icons, and misspelled title text.
Limit the color system to a restrained palette.

title: Ink Double Exposure Poster
description: Chinese ink, portrait, and layered atmosphere composition.
useWhen: Use for poetic portrait posters, ink atmospheres, and layered cultural visuals.
guidance: Blend portrait silhouette, ink texture, atmosphere, and negative space.
Keep composition quiet, premium, and readable.
pitfalls: Avoid cheap fantasy collage and overloaded scenery.
Use subtle text or no text unless required.

title: Nature Science Poster
description: Minimal product-style science posters for natural subjects.
useWhen: Use for natural subjects that need a premium, clean science poster feel.
guidance: Use a clear subject, minimal copy, soft shadows, and disciplined whitespace.
Keep the scientific label short and visible.
pitfalls: Avoid heavy advertising language.
Avoid dense encyclopedia blocks.

title: Product Commerce Visual
description: Product shots, packaging, detail pages, and selling-point layouts.
useWhen: Use for product hero shots, packaging visuals, detail pages, and sales layouts.
guidance: Define product, selling points, material, scene, lighting, and layout blocks.
Separate hero product, benefit labels, and supporting props.
pitfalls: Avoid random props that weaken product recognition.
Constrain packaging text and claim wording.

title: Personalized Beauty Report
description: Recommendation-report layouts for beauty and lifestyle products.
useWhen: Use for beauty recommendations, skin reports, shopping assistants, and lifestyle product cards.
guidance: Use a report-like hierarchy with diagnosis, recommendation, and product cards.
Keep product images, labels, and ratings aligned.
pitfalls: Avoid medical claims and unreadable dense notes.
Keep recommendation logic simple.

title: Brand Identity Package
description: Logo, palette, typography, applications, and brand touchpoints.
useWhen: Use for logo systems, brand boards, visual identity kits, and application mockups.
guidance: Define brand name, positioning, palette, typography, logo usage, and touchpoints.
Ask for a coherent board with aligned applications.
pitfalls: Avoid unrelated logo variants and inconsistent palettes.
Keep brand text accurate.

title: Brand Touchpoint Board
description: Campaign boards across packaging, social, web, and display contexts.
useWhen: Use for multi-touchpoint campaign boards and brand rollout previews.
guidance: Specify touchpoint list, shared visual rules, and mockup arrangement.
Use one palette and one typography logic across all panels.
pitfalls: Avoid mixing many unrelated campaign styles.
Limit touchpoints if readability drops.

title: Architecture & Space
description: Interior, exterior, city, map, and spatial concept visuals.
useWhen: Use for interiors, architecture renders, city maps, spatial plans, and environment concepts.
guidance: Define viewpoint, scale, material, lighting, and spatial function.
For maps, specify landmarks, labels, border decoration, and visual accuracy level.
pitfalls: Avoid impossible perspectives unless the output is conceptual.
Lock map label language and relative placement.

title: Realistic Photography
description: Lens, lighting, film texture, and documentary-style photo prompts.
useWhen: Use for portraits, street photos, product photography, and cinematic realism.
guidance: Specify camera distance, lens, light source, texture, background, and motion.
Use believable imperfections for documentary realism.
pitfalls: Avoid over-polished plastic skin unless commercial beauty is required.
Add negative constraints for hands, text, and anatomy when needed.

title: Street Accident Moment
description: Realistic phone-photo scenes with negative constraints.
useWhen: Use for candid street moments, accidental spills, documentary phone shots, and fast action.
guidance: Describe the exact moment, camera height, motion blur, and street context.
Add negative constraints for staged poses and fake ad lighting.
pitfalls: Avoid too-clean compositions.
Keep the event plausible and grounded.

title: Illustration & Art Style
description: Anime, watercolor, ink, material experiments, and art direction.
useWhen: Use for anime, watercolor, ink, decorative art, and style experiments.
guidance: Define composition, subject, palette, brush material, mood, and rendering depth.
For reference images, state what must be preserved.
pitfalls: Avoid style-only prompts without composition.
Lock character identity when using references.

title: Character Design Sheet
description: Characters, pose sheets, action grids, and identity consistency.
useWhen: Use for character sheets, pose grids, action breakdowns, and identity references.
guidance: Define identity anchors, outfit, proportions, pose count, and sheet layout.
Keep face, hairstyle, and costume details consistent.
pitfalls: Avoid changing costume details between poses.
Limit pose count if the sheet becomes crowded.

title: 3D Collectible Toy
description: Reference photo to premium 3D collectible figure prompts.
useWhen: Use for premium collectible figures, avatar toys, blind-box characters, and 3D display renders.
guidance: Preserve face and outfit anchors from the reference.
Specify material, packaging, base, lighting, and collectible scale.
pitfalls: Avoid generic toy bodies without identity details.
Keep packaging text minimal and accurate.

title: Scene Storytelling
description: Storyboards, worldbuilding, narrative scenes, and emotional pacing.
useWhen: Use for storyboards, worldbuilding, live scenes, and emotional narrative frames.
guidance: Define who, where, when, conflict, emotion, and camera framing.
Use scene details to support narrative rather than decoration.
pitfalls: Avoid generic fantasy backgrounds.
Keep narrative cues visible in the frame.

title: History & Classical Themes
description: Dynasty clothing, scroll narrative, poetry, and traditional motifs.
useWhen: Use for ancient Chinese themes, scrolls, dynasty clothing, poetry visuals, and historical scenes.
guidance: Specify dynasty, clothing system, object references, layout format, and cultural mood.
Use scroll, album page, or poster format deliberately.
pitfalls: Avoid mixing dynasties when historical accuracy matters.
Constrain random modern props.

title: Document & Publishing
description: White papers, manuals, encyclopedic plates, and page systems.
useWhen: Use for white papers, manuals, encyclopedic plates, report pages, and publication systems.
guidance: Define page size, columns, table of contents, figure system, and typography hierarchy.
Use readable headings, tables, labels, and page rhythm.
pitfalls: Avoid tiny dense text.
Keep charts and captions aligned to the page grid.

title: Concept Product Breakdown
description: R&D boards, exploded views, mixed tasks, and special outputs.
useWhen: Use for experimental prompt tasks, R&D boards, exploded diagrams, and unusual visual systems.
guidance: Define the artifact type, components, labels, material logic, and final presentation format.
Use clear callouts and a controlled technical style.
pitfalls: Avoid unspecified mixed tasks.
Keep labels short and component relationships visible.
